The overall macroeconomic environment, national revenue, and budgetary situation,

therefore, do not offer large untapped sources of financing for health. While there are

genuine requirements for additional financing for health, especially to fund frontline

workers, the MOH is already ranked third for expenditure allocations appropriated by

government after the Ministry of Finance and Economic Management (MFEM) and the

Ministry of Education.

Development partners can be helpful, but the main effort must come from

government. Government already relies heavily on development partners to supplement

- and in some cases possibly substitute for - government's own expenditure on health.

Development partners were already providing over one-third (37 percent) of total public

expenditure in 2012, lifting government-appropriated expenditure on health from VT

6,122 ($66.72) per capita to total public expenditure of VT 9,672 ($105.42) per capita.
